newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pacific Andes plans further expansion.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Andes plans further expansion.

text.p: Pacific Andes (Holdings) Ltd said on Tuesday it was planning further expansion of its frozen seafood supply business in China, Eastern Europe and Africa.
Joe Cheng, Pacific Andes finance director, said the company had secured a 35 percent share of the frozen seafood products market in China.
He said this could rise and that Chinese imports of frozen seafood were growing at 25 percent per year.
Cheng said sales in Eastern Europe had risen to Hong Kong $78 million in the six months to September 1996 against sales of HK$3 million in the same period last year.
Frank Ng, Pacific Andes managing director, said competitive seafood prices were fuelling demand.
Ng said diversification into fishing operations would give the company access to additional fish species stocks, helping to broaden its product supply base into salmon and Pacific cod.
"It gives us the opportunity to access the under-utilised stocks," he said. The move would also ensure strong sourcing of good quality, low-cost fish, he added.
The diversification is through a 60 percent-owned subsidiary, Sea Glory Ltd. The remaining 40 percent is held by Russian partners.
Sea Glory is investing US$3.3 million in a refurbished fishing vessel with full on-board processing, production and freezing plant. It is due to go into operation in January 1997.
Sea Glory would initially supply five percent of Pacific Andes' sales. Possible expansion of fishing operations will be reviewed after its first full year, said Cheng.
The news conference followed the announcement of interim profits up 22.6 percent at HK$28.09 million against HK$22.91 million last year.
Singapore-listed Pacific Andes (Holdings) is a unit of Hong-based Pacific Andes International Holdings.
